newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey launches probe over anti-Israel protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkey launches probe over anti-Israel protest.

text.p: Turkey's Interior Ministry has launched an investigation into an Islamist mayor over an anti-Israel protest that upset the secular elite of the country, a ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The investigation was begun yesterday," the official told Reuters.

Anatolian news agency quoted Interior Minister Meral Aksener as saying she would act as necessary against the mayor, who belongs to the senior coalition partner, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party. The ministry official said he could be suspended.

The protest, named "Jerusalem Night", took place last Friday in Ankara's Sincan district and was carried on Turkish news programmes. A speech by Sincan's mayor, Bekir Yildiz, has been criticised in the media as a call for the implementation of the strict Islamic sharia law.

Youths dressed as Palestinians pretended to throw stones at Israeli troops in a play at a public hall in Sincan to mark Jerusalem Day, declared an annual day of protest against Israel by late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

The mayor and the Iranian ambassador spoke on a stage draped with the banners of Fathi Shqaqi, the late leader of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group, and Imam Moussa Sadr, an influential cleric venerated by some Lebanese Shi'ites. Imam Sadr disappeared while on a trip to Libya in the late 1970's.
The foreign ministry summoned Iran's ambassador, Mohammad-Reza Baqeri, to protest against his role in Jerusalem day. Iran objected to Turkey's protest.
A state security court also launched an inquiry into the event while main opposition Motherland Party asked the government for an explanation of the conduct of the Iranian ambassador.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has gone back on promises to scrap a military training accord with Israel that has angered Arab countries and Iran.
But Erbakan has raised the hackles of the secularist wing of his coalition government in recent weeks with plans to build mosques and other Islamist programmes.
